title: Sprint review at the food bank
setting: Agile team building a volunteer-scheduling app for a food bank, in two-week sprints. The narrator is the Scrum Master; the product owner owns the backlog.

steps.line: I'm Ben, Scrum Master for a small team building a volunteer-scheduling app for a food bank. Zara is our product owner.
It's sprint review day. Managers from three food bank sites are joining to see what we built and give feedback.
We won't demo the reminder texts. They didn't meet the definition of done, so I'll say so plainly and they go back to the backlog.
A site manager asks for a printable rota. I don't promise anything. I tell her Zara will look at it with her.
Zara adds the rota idea to the product backlog on the spot, and says she'll order it after hearing from the other sites.
A developer says the sign-up page feels slow. We don't try to fix it here; we note it to look into after the review.
Kemi, from the largest site, talks over the others. I let her finish her point, then ask the other two sites for their view.
We finish ten minutes early. I don't fill the time. I thank everyone and let them go.
I send a short summary: what we showed, what wasn't done and why, and the new backlog ideas.
Tomorrow is the retrospective. The team will pick one thing to improve, and I'll facilitate.
